subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC deployment recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC deployment recap & next steps

Hi Jamie —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to make next steps explicit. Please feel free to correct anything I’ve missed.

High-level goals you shared:
- Move inference for patient-facing summarization and clinical search into an on-prem / VPC-hosted environment to meet data residency and PHI controls.
- Maintain sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for 512-token summaries and support concurrent throughput of ~120 requests/sec initially.
- Keep model behavior consistent with current hosted APIs (no quality regressions) while reducing per-token egress and audit exposure.

Primary pain points / constraints:
- Network: AcmeHealth requires no outbound internet egress from the inference subnet (air-gapped-ish). All model downloads and telemetry must go through a customer-managed bastion or via pre-staged images.
- Compliance: Data residency and PHI handling demands SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management.
- Ops: Tight change-control windows — deployments must be scheduled and we need an installation checklist for security review.

What we agreed on today:
1) Redwood Private (VPC) is the recommended path — private control plane with a customer-managed deployment host or air-gapped on-prem option.
2) We’ll provide a network deployment diagram + an installation checklist by EOD Monday (attachment: redwood-private-vpc-arch-diagram.pdf).
3) Security pack: SOC 2 artifacts and a minimal evidence bundle for your auditors (we’ll send an initial pack for review).
4) Technical POC: 2-week POC targeting 512-token summaries with the quantized model build we discussed. Performance targets and acceptance criteria will be listed in the Mutual Action Plan.
5) Procurement: we noted a typical timeline (30–60 days) once you have Tech & Security sign-off; we’ll prepare a draft MAP and draft SOW to accelerate.

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Camila (Redwood): Send network diagram + installation checklist — by Mon 2026-02-23.
- Camila/Marissa: Share Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and initial SOW draft — by Wed 2026-02-25.
- Jamie / AcmeHealth Security: Share primary security contact and any internal procurement template — when available.
- Michael (Redwood): Prep initial POC config (hardware guidance + quantization profile) — ready before POC start.

Attachments included: redwood-private-vpc-arch-diagram.pdf (network diagram), redwood-security-evidence-pack.zip (SOC 2 / controls), acmehealth-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

If that looks right, I’ll queue the diagram and MAP and we can lock a follow-up for Wednesday to walk the MAP with your Security and Infra teams.

Thanks,
Camila

--
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private VPC deployment recap & next steps

Camila —

Thanks for the thorough recap, that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from Security/Infra side:
- We will not allow outbound internet access from the inference subnet; model artifacts must be delivered over an internal channel or pre-loaded images.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS in our primary region and require an HSM-backed key for production.
- Audit logs: we need retention of 7 years for a subset of request metadata (anonymized ids ok) — can you confirm Redwood supports configurable retention and export?

Next: looping in our IT lead Priya (cc’d) and procurement lead Mark (I’ll forward separately). Can you include a short note in the MAP about handover steps to our change-management process?

Also: can you send the SOC 2 cover letter and the network diagram you mentioned? That will help speed our internal review.

Thanks — Jamie

Great, thanks — a few quick answers inline and next artifacts attached.

- Model delivery: we can support staged image delivery through your bastion or provide an air-gapped install bundle that your infra team can load. We’ll include both options on the MAP.
- KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS + HSM integrations). We’ll list required key policies and an example setup in the checklist.
- Audit logs: configurable retention is supported. For the POC we’ll keep 90-day logs by default and can extend to 7 years per your policy; we’ll include an export path to your SIEM.

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-arch-diagram.pdf, redwood-security-evidence-pack.zip (SOC 2 summary + control matrix), acmehealth-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft).
